system.description:
Broad theoretical knowledge across a wide range of disciplines - biology, history, law, psychology, military tactics, engineering principles, medicine, chemistry, and more. Academic characters are not necessarily specialists; they are people who have read, studied, and retained enough to form useful hypotheses and recognise patterns across fields. Knowledge doesn't guarantee practical execution, but it informs and guides it.

For applied, hands-on practical knowledge, see Mechanics.
system.overcome: Use Academic to recall relevant information, identify a substance, organism, or process, understand a document or technical text, make an educated inference about an unfamiliar situation, or work out what something is and how it probably behaves.
system.caa: Use Academic to establish a useful fact as a scene aspect - Knows the Building's Original Purpose, Recognised the Symptoms, Behavioural Science 101, Hazardous Material Storage.
system.attack: An academic understanding of human physiology might conceivably be useful, but only in extremely specific circumstances, or a specific stunt.
system.defend: Only to maintain a detached, reasonable perspective on human folly as the blows fall.
